title: The Fragility of Jailbreak Robustness Across Operational States
abstract: arXiv:2608.30748v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Existing jailbreak evaluations typically characterize robustness using a single attack success rate (ASR) measured in a default configuration (the vanilla state). However, user-LLM interactions can induce diverse operational states beyond the vanilla state. In this work, we find that jailbreak robustness is highly fragile to operational-state variation: even when the attack remains fixed, changing only an ordinary system prompt not designed to affect safety can dramatically alter attack success rates. We systematically investigate this phenomenon across seven aligned models and three representative jailbreak attacks, observing substantial differences in ASR between vanilla and non-vanilla operational states. In one case, ASR increases by up to 56 percentage points (2% to 58%) solely due to a change in operational state. Remarkably, these increases occur even for attacks originally designed and optimized under vanilla-state evaluation.

translated_title: 跨操作状态的越狱鲁棒性脆弱性研究
translated_abstract: 现有的越狱评估通常使用在默认配置（即“原始状态”）下测得的单一攻击成功率（ASR）来刻画模型鲁棒性。然而，用户与大语言模型的交互可能会引发超出原始状态的多种操作状态。在这项工作中，我们发现越狱鲁棒性对操作状态的变化高度脆弱：即使攻击保持不变，仅改变一个并非旨在影响安全的普通系统提示词，就能显著改变攻击成功率。我们在七个对齐模型和三种代表性越狱攻击上系统地研究了这一现象，观察到原始状态与非原始操作状态之间ASR存在显著差异。在一个案例中，仅由于操作状态的改变，ASR就提升了高达56个百分点（从2%到58%）。值得注意的是，即使是那些最初在原始状态评估下设计和优化的攻击，也会出现这种提升。
tldr: 该论文揭示了大语言模型的越狱鲁棒性对操作状态变化极为脆弱——仅改变一个普通系统提示词即可使攻击成功率提升高达56个百分点，表明现有单一默认配置下的安全评估严重低估了模型的真实风险。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that LLM jailbreak robustness is highly fragile to operational-state variation—merely changing an ordinary system prompt can increase attack success rates by up to 56 percentage points, showing that safety evaluations under a single default configuration severely underestimate real-world risks.
